area: about 2 miles east of the county dump, east Bakersfield
summary: A grass fire roughly 2 miles east of the county dump and north of the railroad tracks grew from 3–5 acres to 5–10 as units arrived. Engine 345, water tender 12, dozers, a safety officer and helicopter 409 made up the response, with crews working access through corral roads off Newmark; Union Pacific train traffic was held while crews mopped up. Crews dubbed it the Apollo Incident.
A fire in an alley across from the 100 block of Bell Avenue spread toward a house and was upgraded to a structure response — Station 64, Truck 1, medic squad 63 and Battalion 6 among the assignment.

area: Copus Road, about 5.5 miles west of Old River Road
summary: A two-vehicle head-on collision on Copus Road roughly 5.5 miles west of Old River Road pulled multiple engines plus a truck; an air ambulance was placed on standby and later stood down, with one ground ambulance cancelled as units handled it.
A vehicle reportedly drove into a building on South Union Avenue, with CHP en route and Battalion 4 dispatched.
A single reporting party reported multiple shots heard; the exact location was unclear on the air as units responded.

A burglary in progress sent units looking for a suspect — a white male, 5-foot-11, about 150 pounds, in a white tank top and black gym shorts — last seen riding a blue beach cruiser and exiting onto Union Avenue.
A fire in a downtown alley spread into a garage, drawing the Station 1 assignment: Engine 1, Truck 1, Rescue 1, Battalion 1 and Engine 6.
A driver fled a stopped vehicle on foot near 3rd & Union and jumped a fence; the passenger was uncooperative and no direction of travel was given at first.
A black Chevy SUV whose driver appeared slumped over, playing loud music and swerving, drew a traffic stop north of Hageman Road; it was thought related to an earlier suspicious-person report.
Two subjects were seen in a recycling yard on Gibson Street digging through material with flashlights; no further description was given.

agency: Kern County Fire Department / Hall Ambulance
summary: A medical aid for an accidental overdose, corrected to a medication error, drew Rescue 6.
A disturbance between family members had medical units responding alongside police for a subject with difficulty breathing.

agency: Kern County Fire Department / Hall Ambulance
summary: A medical aid for traumatic injuries on Silver Street drew a Code 2 response.

agency: Kern County Fire Department / Hall Ambulance
summary: A medical aid for difficulty breathing on Maple Trail.
A medical aid for a seizure at a recovery services building on Baker Street drew Engine 4.
A person in crisis, reportedly nude with a shirt draped over them and possibly mid-psychiatric episode, drew units to 21st & O streets.
A Spanish-speaking caller watching a vacant residence reported unknown subjects in a blue Honda dropping items off before leaving southbound.
Report of a 6-year-old possibly being locked out by someone inside a residence on Jefferson Street.
A disturbance at a business in the 2700 block of White Lane.
A vehicle reportedly not stopping on Highway 99 near the Highway 223 interchange raised the possibility of a pursuit.
A woman reported a man banging on her door while she screamed at him to leave, with the banging audible in the background; a heavy-duty response was requested.
A commercial fire alarm at a downtown building on 18th Street.
A vegetation response on Sierra Highway.
